g.text: Dependency direction: API → Service → Repository → Infrastructure. RLS is the real authorization boundary.
RLS is the real authorization boundary; guards are defence-in-depth.
grantRole(profile : Profile, community : Community, role : MembershipRole) : CommunityMembership
transferPrimaryContact(unit : Unit, to : UnitResidency, by : CommunityMembership) : void
initiate(invoice : Invoice, method : PaymentMethod, payer : Profile) : Payment
refund(payment : Payment, amount : Money, reason : String) : Payment
publish(source, recipients : List<Profile>, channels : Set<NotificationChannel>) : Notification
record(ctx, eventType : String, target, metadata : JSON) : AuditEvent
Services depend on the Repository<T> abstraction, never on the
Supabase SDK (Dependency Inversion). Only repositories & gateways
userClient ⇒ RLS enforced; serviceClient ⇒ RLS bypassed (trusted server code only)
only digests persist; plaintext returned to caller once
hosts RLS policies + EXCLUDE USING gist constraints
DTOs «map to» domain entities in the service layer
Layered architecture — dependency flows downward only
Authorization: Postgres RLS (userClient) is the real boundary;
RoleGuard + RolePolicy are defence-in-depth in the API layer.
